focus_areas: Legibility and correctness of numerical text on the dial.
Physical plausibility of the pointer hands (shadows/thickness).
Consistency of the casing rim thickness.
Objective verification of the absence of mercury column features.
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the text on the dial. AI generators often struggle with small, curved text. Verify if the numbers follow a logical sequence (e.g., 28, 29, 30) or if they degrade into nonsense. Also, examine the pointer hands; do they cast realistic shadows on the dial face, or do they look like flat decals? Check the reflection on the glass cover for consistency with the light source. Crucially, use the open_vocabulary_detector to confirm there are NO vertical glass tubes or mercury columns present, ensuring this is strictly an aneroid barometer.
image_description: A close-up, slightly angled view of a vintage aneroid barometer. The instrument features a circular brass or gold-toned metal casing with a glass cover. The dial face is off-white/cream with black numerical markings (appearing to be in inches of mercury, e.g., 28, 29, 30) and descriptive weather text. There are two pointer hands: a thin black indicator hand and a thicker reference hand. The background is blurred, showing hints of dark wood or furniture.
